newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner mulls foreign investment bank buy.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner mulls foreign investment bank buy.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG said on Tuesday it had no interest in taking over a fellow German financial insitution but was considering an acquisition in the investment banking sector abroad.

Dresdner chief executive Juergen Sarrazin also told a news conference that the bank would like to expand its relationship with German insurance giant Allianz AG, which owns more than 20 percent of Dresdner.
Dresdner said earlier on Tuesday that it was planning a capital raise to allow itself more leeway for strategic moves.

"We are continuing to position ourself abroad, especially in the area of investment banking," Sarrazin said in response to a question about what Dresdner planned to do with the proceeds from the capital raise.
"We are establishing a war chest but not in the sense that we are planning hostile takeovers."

Sarrazin said the capital increase by a nominal 120 million marks, to take place in August, would boost Dresdner's equity capital to more than 16 billion marks from the end-June level of 14.82 billion marks.
Including other capital measures such as the expiry of a warrant bond, Dresdner's equity capital will exceed 17 billion marks by the end of the year.
Sarrazin said the capital increase was not linked to the planned mega-merger of Bavarian banks Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG announced last week.

Dresdner, which will be relegated from second to third-largest bank in Germany as a result of the merger, will be different from the new Bavarian giant because Dresdner is positioning itself globally, Sarrazin said.

"We are not completely different, but we are different," he said. "International orientation has a special significance at Dresdner. We regard ourselves as a global player in various areas such as asset management."
However the two banks would be in direct competition in the property finance business, which accounted for a quarter of Dresdner's balance sheet total, Sarrazin added.
Sarrazin also said Dresdner planned to intensify its cooperation with Allianz beyond their current cooperation in insurance and the distribution of insurance policies.
"In our link with Allianz there will definitely be close cooperation in other areas of the financial services sector, and we are thinking about that," Sarrazin said.
The two were considering cooperating more closely on asset management, mortgage banking and distribution, Sarrazin said.
"That's a decisive factor in our strategic thinking."
